title: Claude Mastery Track

modules.title: Learn Claude by fixing your real issues

lessons.title: Learn Claude by fixing your real issues

blocks.text: You don't study Claude separately. Every ticket you fix is a practice round. After each one, you notice what you had to repeat or correct, save it in the right place, and the next ticket starts smarter. Over a few weeks, that loop is what mastery looks like.
The amber step is the one people skip. Asking "what did I have to repeat?" after every ticket is what turns ordinary use into skill.
Every ticket touches every stage, so one ticket can practise several skills at once. You don't need a separate exercise for each.

lessons.title: Watch, drill, use: 45 minutes a day

blocks.text: Anthropic's free courses are the videos. The commands below are the ones worth memorising. The real learning happens when you use them on that day's ticket.
20 min**Watch**One lesson from the course for this week (table below). Pause and try each thing it shows in a real repo.
5 min**Drill**Run the flashcards below for this week's commands. Mark the ones you knew; repeat the rest tomorrow.
20 min**Use**Use at least 3 of this week's commands on your actual ticket. A command you've used 3 times stays with you.

items: Claude Code has 100+ commands. About 35 cover daily work, so those are on this page.
You never need to remember the full list: type `/` to see every command, and `?` on an empty prompt for shortcuts.
Add one week's group at a time. Don't start Week 2 commands until Week 1 ones come without thinking.

blocks.text: 5-minute drill
Sources: commands reference, shortcuts, CLI reference, Anthropic Academy. Checked 2 Nov 2026; the list changes with releases, so run `/release-notes` now and then.
About one skill every two to three days. If a week is busy with on-call, the next week waits; there's no deadline.
Week 1**Talk to it well**1 Brief · 2 ContextEvery prompt in task / files / done shape. One topic finished across two sessions.
Week 2**Make rules stick**3 CLAUDE.md · 4 Plan modeRepo CLAUDE.md for ONCALL. PD carousel fix planned before it's coded.
Week 3**Build the crew**5 Sub-agents · 7 Hookscode-locator, reviewer and the 4 guardrail hooks (agent Phases 1–2).
Week 4**One command**6 Skills · 8 MCP + costWrite /resolve, scope MCPs per agent, read your usage.
Build and use these on real tickets before the other seven. The rest follow the same pattern with different rules and tools.
**code-locator**Simplest kind: read-only, cheap model. Teaches the `description`, `tools` and `model` fields, and how a brief shapes the answer.
**reviewer**Teaches why a fresh context matters. It catches what the agent that wrote the code can't see.
**debugger**Hardest. Teaches passing evidence between you, the device and the agent.
The single biggest lever on result quality

rows: Three lines: the task, the files or area, and what done looks like. Add the constraint that matters most (e.g. "don't touch shared libraries").
Agents only know their brief. A vague brief to code-locator gets a vague file list; "PD page, Monsoon carousel, which of Lumen `:767` or Harmonix `:665` renders on a Harmonix build" gets an answer.

rows: MCP servers connect Jira, Figma, Postman, groundcover and dart. Each server's tool list costs context, and each model costs differently.
You turned most MCPs off to save context. Scoping them per agent gets the tools back without the cost, and your earlier usage drain came from a scheduled task, which `ccusage` would have shown.

modules.title: The one habit that makes it stick

lessons.title: The one habit that makes it stick

blocks.text: After every ticket: what did I repeat, or remind Claude about?
Whatever it was gets a permanent home, so you never type it again.
A command or path you retyped**repo CLAUDE.md**
A rule it must never break**hook**
A rule for one kind of work**that agent's file**
